name: lightmem
description: Wraps LightMem (zjunlp/LightMem, MIT, ICLR 2026, arXiv:2510.18866, "LightMem: Lightweight and Efficient Memory-Augmented Generation"): ingests a conversation via a topic-segmentation stage (an attention-based encoder that groups consecutive turns into coherent topics before spending any LLM calls on them) followed by LLM-driven metadata/fact extraction into embedding-indexed memory entries, with an 'offline' consolidation update pass that merges/prunes near-duplicate entries in the background rather than on every write -- the paper's actual efficiency contribution versus mem0/A-MEM-style baselines it's benchmarked against (in its own README, on the same kind of long-conversation QA task this repo targets). NOT a prompted-LLM baseline by itself for the extraction/consolidation steps -- those go through dialogue_benchmarks.llm.complete()/embed() via two small subclasses overriding LightMem's own OpenAI-shaped manager/embedder classes; final QA-answer generation over retrieved memories is this Method's own completion call, same pattern as mem0/a_mem/memoryos. Vendored (vendor/lightmem/, no usable PyPI release -- the real `lightmem` PyPI name is squatted by an unrelated placeholder package). Fixed one real upstream bug (self.compressor referenced before being set when pre_compress=False and topic_segment=True -- confirmed by actually constructing LightMemory with that combination). See method.py's module docstring for the full mechanism, licensing, and verification notes.
author: Wnsdnl
